chapter_note: This chapter is heavily damaged (60.9%). It opens with an extended biographical narrative frame — Mani at the Tigris in Sapores' kingdom witnessing a flood with lions, prompting a disciple's question about the "garment/cloak of the lions." The substrate teaching begins around seg 36 with the First Man bearing the elements, standing against the Enmity in Darkness, and the archons receiving the garment of lions. The teaching describes a primordial cosmic flood-judgment river of which the Tigris flood is a tiny mirror. Lots of dialogue framing wraps the cosmology. The biographical narrative (lions of Tigris in Sapores' day) is purely apostolic-dialogue narrative frame; the cosmological core (First Man / Enmity / Archons / great river of Judgment) is genuinely old substrate material.
